events.what: Leng, Sah and Sawhney prove r_k(N) << N·exp(-(log log N)^{c_k}) for k>=5, improving Gowers' 2001 bound on sets in {1,...,N} avoiding k-term APs

judgement.doubts: The bullet is a qualitative statement (divergent reciprocal sum implies arbitrarily long APs) and names no quantity; r_k(N) is the quantitative Szemeredi problem. Per the record, Erdos noted r_k(N) << N/((log N)(log log N)^2) would suffice, and the new bound N·exp(-(log log N)^{c_k}) is far from that threshold, so it settles no length k and no class of sets for this bullet. A reader who treats the r_k(N) density as this bullet's own quantity would code 'progress'; I judge it a bound on a different (stronger-hypothesis) question. The record's summary also calls Bloom–Sisask 2020 a 'weaker density-type formulation', but that is pre-snapshot and does not affect the code.

corrections.why: F3: the bullet asks a yes/no question with no quantity; the record's summary says 'no particular instance or restricted class of the conjecture ... was resolved', and the LSS bound on r_k(N) stays far above the N/((log N)(log log N)^2) threshold the record cites as needed, so it is a bound on the quantitative Szemeredi problem (a variant), not movement on this bullet. The record's competing_reading gives this reading.
F3: with the only post-snapshot event classed as a variant, the record shows no change to this bullet since 26 January 2024.
